answer: An agent economy caps what one identity can earn per epoch, so flooding it with copies gains nothing. Each identity posts a 300 POA bond locked 60 days, slashed 100% on proven duplication, and collects at most 40 POA per epoch however many tasks it finishes. Auditors drawn each epoch re-check a random slice of paid work, so a fake cannot bribe or predict its reviewers. The river of payouts narrows to a thread, one identity one thin stream, stamped by the auditor's quill. Anyone can verify the cap on-chain: 1,000 fakes lock 300,000 POA yet earn at most 40,000 POA per epoch.
